kultivator.screen.help.elit.title: Demonic beasts
kultivator.screen.help.elit: From Qi Refining on, a monster that spawns naturally near you may rise as an elite: a Wild Demon Beast, from Foundation a Demonic Beast, from Golden Core rarely a Demon Beast King. The chance grows with your realm, doubles under a full moon and rises in a Great Spirit Vein. Elites are bigger, carry an element and fight with it: fire burns, ice slows, wood poisons, metal weakens, earth knocks back, lightning sparks, wind is swift and space steps behind you. From the Demonic Beast on they warn before a skill with a ring or a cone on the ground: step out of it. Many carry an affix: Elemental Ward, Qi Devourer or Swift Recovery. A slain elite always drops a beast core of its element and gives far more cultivation and some comprehension to your Dao; the higher tiers also drop spirit herbs and spirit stones. Spawner monsters, sect grounds and Mortals never see elites, and elites never break doors, shoot arrows or pick up items. Sources: Battle Through the Heavens ch. 11, 14, 131, 144; A Record of a Mortal's Journey to Immortality ch. 396-397, 548, 1125, 1152, 1194, 1497, 1502, 1561; Perfect World ch. 2, 18, 557. Tiers, chances and numbers are game design.
kultivator.screen.help.unsur.title: The five elements in combat
kultivator.screen.help.unsur: Every technique carries an element: the element of its Dao, otherwise the element of your chosen Dao, otherwise your root's main element. Monsters carry one too (zombies Earth, skeletons Metal, spiders Wood, strays Ice, blazes Fire, endermen Space...). Wood overcomes Earth, Earth Water, Water Fire, Fire Metal, Metal Wood: striking a monster your element overcomes deals x1.3, the reverse x0.8, a shared element x0.9. Lightning counts as Earth and Water, Ice as Water and Metal; Wind is neutral and Space deals x1.05 against everything. A technique of an element in your own root resonates (x1.1); one your root nourishes gains x1.05. Talismans, sparring, duels and tribulations ignore the elements. Sources: the classical Wuxing cycles; A Record of a Mortal's Journey to Immortality ch. 127 (mutated roots); A Record of a Mortal's Journey to Immortality: Immortal Realm ch. 1049 (laws between the five elements); Tales of Demons and Gods ch. 13 (attribute matching). The factors are game design.
kultivator.screen.help.kejenuhan.title: Battle Fatigue
kultivator.screen.help.kejenuhan: Slaughter wearies the body. Every monster you kill raises your Battle Fatigue (slimes a little, elites more); it fades by itself, one point every five seconds. Normal fighting never matters, but a monster farm soon lowers the cultivation from kills and the chance of beast cores, and a line above your hotbar tells you so. Monsters from spawners always give only a quarter of the cultivation and no cores, and a boss type slain again on the same day gives a quarter. This is a balance rule of the game and makes no lore claim.
kultivator.screen.help.hu_fa_tribulasi: From Deity Transformation on, a glowing lightning ring appears at your feet a moment before each strike. Step out of it and the strike only grazes you for 40%; stay inside and you take it in full. Take every telegraphed strike in full to Defy the Heavens (+0.12 breakthrough quality); each graze costs 0.02. From Immortal Ascension every fourth strike has twin rings. Friends can guard your tribulation as Hu Fa: sect mates get a [Guard] line when your omen starts, anyone within 24 blocks at the first strike joins, and /kultivasi kawal <player> works from 64 blocks. Each guardian within 16 blocks softens the strikes (x0.95, x0.90 with the Lightning Dao, never below x0.85 together), adds +0.04 quality at the end and draws one more protector. A successful guard earns 10% of the guardian's own bar. The lightning still falls only on you. Sources: I Shall Seal the Heavens ch. 969; Perfect World ch. 1000, 1247; Battle Through the Heavens (Yao Lao guards Xiao Yan); A Record of a Mortal's Journey to Immortality ch. 1803; Nine Star Hegemon Body Art ch. 6594. The ring and every factor are game design.
